title: Nina the Starry Bride
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Nina, an orphan who steals to survive, is sold or abducted for her rare blue eyes and taken by Prince Azure to impersonate the late princess-priestess Alisha. Trained to play the princess and promised to a foreign fiancé, she resists quietly while feelings grow between her and Azure (Kodansha blurb; ANN Manga Guide). It won the Kodansha Manga Award for shoujo.
life_message: Loyalty and love can grow even inside a role forced on you, and wit is a way to keep your self.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Nina keeps her self-respect quietly rather than by open defiance (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Court manners and royal duty constrain Nina; she adapts rather than rebels.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Royal family and succession disputes drive politics (MU).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Princes, priestess-princess and arranged royal marriage (blurb, MU).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Begins in theft for survival; feelings constrained by duty.

folkways.japan: A Japanese shoujo/josei court romance set in a fictional Middle Eastern-influenced kingdom, using common Japanese romance tropes of a hidden identity and love across rank.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers call it familiar, well-handled trope work; no moralizing noted.
delivery.note: Values come through Nina's choices within a court drama rather than stated themes.

winners_losers: Nina gains status and affection; sympathy rests with her and, increasingly, with Azure.
